To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the companies having substantial investments in intangible assets are more likely to record higher profitability than the companies with low or moderate investments.
the higher the intangible assets, the higher are the margins.
the higher the intangible assets of the companies, the higher their profitability is, provided the investments in the intangibles are over 10% of the sales.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of how much the companies within Central and Eastern Europe should invest in intangible assets to record higher profitability and what is the optimal level of investment.
the relationship between intangible assets and firm performance in CEE countries.
the relationship between the innovation potential of the companies and their financial performance, measured by profitability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the companies investing in the intangible capital, which is the proxy for innovation, are more profitable, but the effect is visible only when the investments are substantial.
higher innovation potential leads to better financial performance only if the company invests in intangible assets substantially.
companies should not be reluctant to invest in innovation as the effect of higher profitability is visible, however, the companies should be careful not to overinvest in the intangibles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the higher innovation potential of the firm does not automatically lead to higher profitability, but the higher investment in intangibles is necessary to generate higher profitability.
the firms having higher innovation potential are able to record superior performance.
the firms having higher innovation potential are able to achieve higher profitability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
companies in CEE region are able to generate superior financial performance if they are willing to invest more in intangibles, but only if their investments are significant.
the companies should not be discouraged to invest in the intangibles.
companies in Central and Eastern Europe can benefit from higher investment in innovation.
